thread:
maria-support: heads up — multiple customers in us-east-3 are reporting 502/504 spikes on hosted inference routes (model=r-instruct-xl). seeing big tail latencies and retries in their logs. escalating.

daniel-oncall: thanks — is this regional or cross-AZ? any pattern in pods/hosts?
maria-support: looks cross-az. error rate jumps when traffic goes to az3-b -> az3-c paths. Support captured a customer repro showing repeated grpc timeouts then 502 from gateway. logs attached to the ticket: s3://internal-logs/incidents/3000001234/trace-1.pcap.gz (access perms applied).
ingrid-runtime: perf graphs show huge KV cache miss rate during the window, followed by a flurry of backend reconnects. misses -> request amplification -> some front-tier connections hit our idle timeout.
raj-network: I see asymmetric RTTs between az3-b and az3-c in our metrics (inflight median RTT az3-b->az3-c ~ 30ms vs az3-c->az3-b ~ 120ms) and retransmit counters are elevated on the az3-b egress. Could be provider-level microbursts or a bad ECMP path.
maria-support: customers also report billing spikes because their clients retry on 5xx -> token usage ballooned. customer-ops is included to coordinate credits. :frowning:

customer-ops: noted, prepping credits template. focus first on mitigation and repro.
daniel-oncall: mitigation options: 1) steer traffic away from az3-c via routing policy (canary alter route) 2) route affected customers to dedicated pools if available 3) raise front-tier timeouts temporarily to avoid killing in-flight requests. preferences?
ingrid-runtime: we should avoid increasing client-facing timeouts broadly. prefer steering/traffic-splitting for affected customer IDs and pin their requests to az3-b host pool. we can also enable aggressive prefix KV caching for their project to reduce backend load.

raj-network: quick test: can you run this from a box in az3-b and az3-c and paste results?
raj-network: traceroute/tcp to gateway ip then run curl to reproduce. example curl we used against customer's dataset:

raj-network: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  --resolve api.redwood.test:443:10.3.45.21 \\n  -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate \\n  -d '{"model":"r-instruct-xl","input":"short prompt"}' \
  --http2 --max-time 15
```

maria-support: from az3-b the request completes in ~0.4s. from az3-c the same command sees a 6-8s handshake + TLS retransmits then a 502.
sre-bot: automated alert: az3 egress retransmit rate exceeded threshold (window=5m) — incident=INC-3000001234 — link=/alerts/INC-3000001234
daniel-oncall: raj, can you check provider AS paths and any recent BGP changes for az3-c uplinks in the last 30m? also check ECMP hash churn.

raj-network: checking — no BGP withdraws in the last 60m, but I do see one transit peer reporting interface errors on their internal dashboard around t+18m. raising with provider now. opened ticket PRV-8921.

ingrid-runtime: operationally, I'll push a temporary route preference for the frontend LB to prefer az3-b egress for requests originated from az3 region for 15m. That should cut the asymmetric RTT exposure.
maria-support: implemented route preference at 3000001375. early signs: error rate for affected customers dropping ~70% in last 5m.

customer-ops: I've drafted the customer note and applied one-off credits for 3 customers. will hold until we stabilize.
daniel-oncall: good. next steps: raj to get provider confirmation and ETA, ingrid to revert route preference after provider fix, verify KV cache hit rate stays healthy, and official postmortem. assign owners.

raj-network: provider responded — transient fiber flap in their metro ring, now rerouted. they estimate full path stabilization 20–30m. ticket updated PRV-8921.

ingrid-runtime: rechecking runtime — KV cache back to baseline, connection churn down. I'll schedule a controlled revert at t+40m and keep canary on.
maria-support: closing customer tickets when stable, continuing monitoring. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
